- A triage owner on Redwood side (name and contact)

Subject: Re: Connector failures after runtime patch — immediate help needed

Thanks — I'm on this. Quick findings after an initial look at the log: the failures surface during long-context token compaction where kernel selection falls back to an experimental quantized path. We've seen a regression in the runtime's kernel-selection heuristics that can trigger memory spikes for connectors with many concurrent short-lived sessions (your pattern).

Workaround (fast): pin workloads to the stable model variant that uses the legacy kernel selection. On your side run:

1) set MODEL_VARIANT=rwd-connector-stable-202605
2) restart connector process: systemctl restart rwd-connector

That should drop error rates immediately while we prepare a proper patch. If you prefer, we can run a rollback from our side.

I'll attach a minimal diff that forces the fallback to the stable kernel (temporary). If you want to test the quick config change, let me know and I can stay on the call.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Attachment: workaround_patch.diff (text, 8KB)
